items.q: How much more code do developers write with autonomous agents, and how much faster do they ship?
items.a: About **741% more code**, but only **~30% faster shipping**.

items.q: Why can't humans just review agent code faster?
items.a: Review accuracy falls off after about **450 lines per hour**, so a 10,000-line diff would take **about a week**.

items.q: What happened when four AI code reviewers checked the same code?
items.a: Each found real bugs, but **none of the same bugs**: run several, don't trust one.

items.q: What happens to the pass rate when you ask 'would the maintainer merge this?' instead of 'does it pass tests?'
items.a: It falls from **87% to 54%**: the maintainer holds an unwritten **sense of good**.

items.q: What does the theory of constraints predict for agentic coding?
items.a: Fix the review bottleneck and it **moves** to ops, then security, until it hits one agents **can't pass**.

items.q: Why does 'keep track of my orders' not define software?
items.a: A bakery, a parts store and a factory need **completely different** software; that knowledge lives **in the customer's head**.

items.q: Which work does Voss bet agents won't take?
items.a: **Deciding what to build**, **defining what good means**, and making it delightful.
Someone who **finds out what people need**, defines good, and **ships with agents doing the typing**.

items.q: Why are junior engineers hit hardest?
items.a: Their training ladder, **well-specified tickets plus feedback**, is now **what we give agents**.

items.q: Which code should humans still review?
items.a: Your **high blast radius code**; delegate everything **cheap to verify**.

items.q: Where should your best people's judgment go?
items.a: Into **specs, rubrics and evals** that agents can use.

items.q: What should you measure instead of lines of code?
items.a: **What actually ships**, reviewer-comment uptake, and the **tests-pass vs would-merge gap**.
